answer: Each agent identity must lock a bond for months and build a public work log that cannot be copied to a new account. Forging duplicates is like stacking shale: every layer costs fresh quarrying, and a copied history leaves a visible seam. A sybil cluster also sends up a plume of identical registration transactions, easy to flag before it earns trust. As the tide of fake accounts rises, slashing burns their bonds faster than they can recoup, so duplication loses money.
